newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Friday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly again today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were narrowly mixed but bond prices were steady to easier. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.17/2.12 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.15/2.10 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.68/1.63 percent against 1.72/1.67 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.23/99.28 from Thursday's close of S$99.25/99.30.
September 2001 was unchanged from Thursday's close of $S99.23/99.28 and June 2003 unchanged at S$98.83/98.88.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent versus Thursday's 3 2-7/8 percent.
